## 1. London Crime Dataset

### 1.1 Load dataset 'London Crime Rate'

Original Data Set download from Kaggle:
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jboysen/london-crime?resource=download

The objects in 'LondonCrimeRate.RData' includes annual incidents of 9 major crime categories from 2008 to 2016 in 33 London boroughs. To see more details about monthly incidents or minor categories, please download the original data set.

The annual population density is attached by variable 'london'. Original Data set download from: 'housing density':
https://data.london.gov.uk/dataset/land-area-and-population-density-ward-and-borough


```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Load objects in LondonCrimeRate.RData into workspace
load(file = "data/LondonCrimeRate.RData")

# list of 33 boroughs
unique(london_crime.rate$borough)

# view the data set london_crime.rate
view(london_crime.rate)
```

### 1.2 Use London geometry information to calculate the weighting matrix W

The shape file for London boroughs is download from:
https://data.london.gov.uk/dataset/statistical-gis-boundary-files-london

The geometry information is needed to calculate the weighting matrix 'W'

```{r}
library(spdep)
load(file = 'data/LondonMap.RData')

# choose K nearest neighbours for spatial weights
#col.knn <- knearneigh(centroids, k = 3)
#nblist <- knn2nb(col.knn)
#nblist <- nblist[-33]
#W <- nb2mat(nblist)


london_map <- subset(london_map, NAME != "City of London")
nb_object <- poly2nb(london_map)
W <- nb2mat(nb_object, style = "W")

image(W)
apply(W, 1, sum)
```

### 1.3 Take logarithms of incidents

```{r}
london_crime.rate <- london_crime.rate %>% 
  group_by(borough, year,major_category) %>%
  mutate(log.Incidents = log(Incidents))

london_crime.rate <- london_crime.rate %>% 
  group_by(borough, major_category) %>%
  mutate(log.diff = log.Incidents - lag(log.Incidents))

# Drop the NA of data set, for borough 'City of London' and crime category 'Sexual Offences', 'Fraud or Forgery' there are all NA
unique(london_crime.rate$major_category)
tmp <- subset(london_crime.rate, borough != 'City of London' & major_category != 'Sexual Offences' & major_category != 'Fraud or Forgery' & year != 2008)
```

```{r}
crime <- array(tmp$log.diff, dim = c(32,8,7),
               dimnames = list(unique(london_crime.rate$borough[london_crime.rate$borough != 'City of London']),
                               2009:2016,
                               unique(london_crime.rate$major_category[london_crime.rate$major_category != 'Sexual Offences' & london_crime.rate$major_category != 'Fraud or Forgery']) ))

# Array Transposition, n * p * t: borough * crime category * time
crime <- aperm(crime,c(1,3,2))
```

## 3. Multiple dimenssion qml Model Test

```{r}

qml_vec_spARCH <- function(Y, W, parameters){

  dimY <- dim(Y)

  n    <- dimY[1]

  p    <- dimY[2]

  t    <- dimY[3]

  dimW <- dim(W)

  if(dimW[1] != n | dimW[2] != n){

    stop("Dimension of W is wrong")

  }


  if(parameters$errortype == "norm"){

    E_logsq_errors <- (digamma(1) - log(2))

    lnsig_u        <-  4.934 # var(logsq(rnorm(50000000)))

  } else if (parameters$errortype == "t"){

    E_logsq_errors <- -0.901 # mean(logsq(rt(50000000, 3)))

    lnsig_u        <-  5.870 # var(logsq(rt(50000000, 3)))

  }


  logsq <- function(x){

    return(log(x^2))

  }


  logsq_back <- function(x, sgn){

    return(sgn*sqrt(exp(x)))

  }


  vec <- function(x){

    return(as.vector(x))

  }

# for 'norm' type, lnsig_u <- 4.934
  LogLikelihood <- function(pars, Y, W, lnsig_u){


    dimY <- dim(Y)

    n    <- dimY[1]

    p    <- dimY[2]

    t    <- dimY[3] 


    A_tilde <- pars[1] * matrix(rep(1, n*p), n, p)

    Psi     <- matrix(pars[2:(p^2+1)], p, p) 

    Pi      <- matrix(pars[(p^2+2):(2*p^2+1)], p, p) 


    S         <- diag(n*p) - t(Psi) %x% W

    log_det_S <- determinant(S, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus


    sum_eps_2 <- 0

    for(i.t in 2:t){

      vec_u_t   <- S %*% vec(logsq(Y[,,i.t])) - vec(A_tilde) - (diag(p) %x% logsq(Y[,,i.t-1])) %*% vec(Pi)

      sum_eps_2 <- sum_eps_2 + sum(vec_u_t^2)

    }

    

    LL <- -1/2 * log(2*pi) + (n * lnsig_u) / (2*p) + (t-1)/(n*p) * log_det_S - 1/(2*n*p*lnsig_u) * sum_eps_2

    

    return((-1) * LL) # ((t-1)*n*p) *

  }


  start_a   <- 1

  start_Psi <- matrix(c(0.5, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5), 2, 2) 

  start_Pi  <- matrix(c(0.3, 0, 0, 0.3), 2, 2) 


  start_pars <- c(start_a, vec(start_Psi), vec(start_Pi))


  out <- solnp(start_pars, fun = LogLikelihood, Y = Y, W = W, lnsig_u = lnsig_u, control = list(trace = FALSE)) # , eqfun = constraint, eqB = 0)
  

  A_est         <- (out$pars[1] - E_logsq_errors) * matrix(rep(1, n*p), n, p)

  Psi_est       <- matrix(out$pars[2:(p^2+1)], p, p) 

  Pi_est        <- matrix(out$pars[(p^2+2):(2*p^2+1)], p, p) 

  
  return(list(A_est = A_est, Psi_est = Psi_est, Pi_est = Pi_est, H = out$hessian, ll = out$values[length(out$values)]))

}
```

```{r}
library("Rsolnp")

qml_vec_spARCH(crime, W, parameters = list(errortype = "norm"))



```
